hooks.text: We could make this lotion for a fraction of what it costs us. There's one ingredient we'd have to swap to do it.
hooks.evidence: Animating question from voice-and-pov.md: 'If a cheaper substitute would do the same job, would we use it?'

hooks.text: Every lotion that ever felt greasy on you had the same ingredient doing it, and it wasn't the one you think.
hooks.evidence: jojoba entry: mineral oil and petrolatum 'form an occlusive film'. Withholds the carrier for the script.

hooks.text: Watch my hand. I want to show you what an emulsifier actually does, because nobody explains this part.
hooks.evidence: Mechanism-forward is the house tone. Pure demo, no claim in the hook.

hooks.text: People ask why our lotion doesn't feel like the drugstore one. That's not an accident. It's a decision, and it cost us margin.
hooks.evidence: 'we paid more for X because Y' — the signature construction

hooks.text: There's an ingredient we get asked to add every year. It would make this cheaper, more consistent and more shelf-stable. We keep saying no.
hooks.evidence: jojoba + emulsifying wax entries: cheaper substitutes are 'more uniform', 'more shelf-stable'

hooks.text: Somebody commented that coconut oil is comedogenic. They're right, and I'm not going to argue with them. I'd rather tell you what's actually in the bottle.
hooks.evidence: Comedogenic fear — 6 mentions. Voice rule: don't moralize, trust the customer to draw conclusions.

hooks.text: If coconut oil reliably breaks you out, don't buy our lotion. I'd rather say that now than take the order.
hooks.evidence: 'Who we're not for' — 5 mentions. Founder integrity does what a customer disclaimer can't.

hooks.text: The average person puts a hundred and twelve different ingredients on their skin before leaving the house. I'm not going to tell you that's dangerous. I'm going to tell you what it makes impossible.
hooks.evidence: EWG / Morning Consult, 2,200 US adults, 2023, via brand-kit category_ingredient_load

hooks.text: There are six things in this bottle and I can tell you why every one of them is in there. It's the sixth that people ask about.
hooks.evidence: Founder narrative: 'the least number of ingredients possible, every one of them earning its place'

hooks.text: This company exists because I turned over a box in my own bathroom and read the warning on the back.
hooks.evidence: Sean's actual origin story, verbatim from founder-narrative.md — the toothpaste 'do not swallow' moment

hooks.text: Our family wanted products where we could confirm every single ingredient. That turned out to be much harder to buy than to make.
hooks.evidence: founder-narrative.md, opening paragraph

hooks.text: Unscented and fragrance-free are not the same word. One of them means something was added, and we had to pick one.
hooks.evidence: Scent appears in ~26 reviews; 4 mentions of buying for a scent-intolerant person

hooks.text: We don't put the word natural on this bottle. There are products labeled natural with SLS in them — the word isn't regulated and it doesn't do any work.
hooks.evidence: voice-and-pov.md, 'The natural trap'. Competitor deliberately not named — the point survives without the fight.

hooks.text: The texture of our lotion shifts batch to batch and we're not going to fix it. It costs us reviews and we're keeping it.
hooks.evidence: Live PDP + coconut oil entry: 'texture variation is a downstream cost of using oil that hasn't been stripped'

hooks.text: Thirty dollars for a bottle of body lotion. I know exactly how that sounds. Give me forty seconds and I'll tell you where it goes.
hooks.evidence: Hard budget ceiling around $15 — 4 mentions

hooks.text: We could make more money on this bottle tomorrow. There are four ingredients we'd swap, and most people wouldn't notice for a month.
hooks.evidence: All four cheap substitutes named in ingredient-stories.json: refined coconut oil, mineral oil, PEG emulsifier, parabens

hooks.text: Out of everything our family makes, one product brings back more repeat customers than all the others put together. It wasn't the one we expected.
hooks.evidence: Measured: 29.2% first-time-buyer repurchase, more returning revenue than every other SKU combined

hooks.text: Nurses, chefs, dishwashers, massage therapists — you all send us the same message, and it changed what we recommend.
hooks.evidence: Occupational trigger — 4 mentions, including a massage therapist's review

hooks.text: Every October our inbox changes. Same message, different people, and it starts the week it gets cold.
hooks.evidence: Cold weather is when the search starts — 5 mentions

hooks.text: A customer wrote that ours is THE moisturizer for Wisconsin winters for her whole family. I didn't write that line, and I couldn't have.
hooks.evidence: Real review, quoted exactly

bodies.name: The oil we didn't use
lines: Most lotion is mostly water and a thickener. That's why you can still feel it on your skin an hour later — it never went anywhere.
The cheap way to fix that is mineral oil, or petrolatum. A fraction of the cost, perfectly uniform every batch, and it would do very good things for our margins.
It also sits on top of your skin. That film is the thing you're feeling. It's extremely good at making a lotion seem like it's working.
We use jojoba instead. Jojoba is technically a wax ester, and its structure is close enough to what your own skin already makes that skin takes it in rather than wearing it.
That's the whole difference. It was never the coconut oil. It's the carrier.
Thirty seconds, and I can put a shirt on.
If a cheaper ingredient did the same job, we'd use it. That one doesn't.

bodies.name: Six things, and why each one is there
lines: The average adult uses twelve personal care products a day, made with as many as a hundred and twelve different ingredients. That's EWG and Morning Consult, twenty-two hundred US adults, 2023.
I'm not going to tell you that's dangerous. I don't know that, and neither does anybody selling you the alternative.
What I'll tell you is that our family couldn't verify a hundred and twelve of anything. That's the actual reason this company exists.
So there are six. Purified spring water. Organic virgin coconut oil. Organic jojoba. A plant-based emulsifying wax. Organic grapefruit seed extract. Organic red palm oil.

The wax is the one worth explaining. The industry standard is a PEG emulsifier — cheaper, more shelf-stable, easier to formulate with. We use a plant-derived one that costs us more to do the identical job.

And the red palm oil is unrefined, which is why it has a colour. Refined palm oil is bleached white, and the antioxidants come out with the colour. If we used that, there'd be no reason to have palm oil in here at all.
Six things. You can read the whole label in about four seconds. That was the brief.

bodies.name: Where thirty dollars goes
lines: Thirty dollars for body lotion. The number in most people's head is fifteen, so let me do this properly.
Most lotion is mostly water. You are paying for dilution, and a thickener that makes it feel like more than it is.
We could get this bottle cheaper tomorrow. Refined coconut oil instead of cold-pressed. Mineral oil instead of jojoba. A PEG emulsifier. Parabens instead of grapefruit seed extract.
Every one of those is cheaper, more consistent and more shelf-stable than what we use. Most people wouldn't notice for a month.
We didn't make those swaps. This is a premium product and we're not going to compromise that for margin.
Here's the number I actually care about. Of everyone who bought this as their first order, twenty-nine percent came back and bought it again — the highest of anything we make.
And you get thirty days. If you don't like it, email us and we refund you. You don't send it back.

ctas.name: The plain ask
ctas.text: We make it, we ship it, it's on realskincare.com. Pure Unscented if you react to things, Coconut Breeze if you don't. Go and get it.

ctas.text: Take thirty days with it. If you don't like it, email us and we'll refund you — and you don't have to send it back. We'd rather do that than keep an order you regret. Link's in my bio.

ctas.name: The first-order nudge
ctas.text: If it's your first order, use SHIPFREE at checkout — shipping's free over twenty-five dollars and this is thirty, so you're covered. realskincare.com, link's in the bio.
